subject.title: [Feature]: Add portable Agent Bundles for export/import across OpenClaw instances

question: Should OpenClaw define a first-party non-secret portable Agent Bundle format, and should it live as a core agent import/export surface, a per-agent backup/restore mode, or a plugin/bundle contract?
rationale: The request changes CLI and Gateway surfaces, config mutation, workspace copying, skill installation, bindings/model settings, and secret/session exclusions, so the permanent owner boundary and security contract need maintainer intent before a safe implementation PR.

options.title: Define scoped native Agent Bundles
options.body: Add a core-owned manifest plus export/import dry-run flow for portable non-secret agent configuration, with explicit allowlists and no credentials, sessions, logs, caches, or device state.

options.title: Fold into per-agent backup/restore
options.body: Route the work through the per-agent backup/restore/clone tracker and add a non-secret portable mode there instead of a separate agent-bundle namespace.

options.title: Keep core APIs only
options.body: Expose only missing generic seams in core and route distributable package formats to ClawHub or plugin bundle contracts.

recommendation.title: Define scoped native Agent Bundles
recommendation.body: Add a core-owned manifest plus export/import dry-run flow for portable non-secret agent configuration, with explicit allowlists and no credentials, sessions, logs, caches, or device state.

likelyOwner.reason: Their recent agent routing and backup-safety history best matches the config, binding, and import/export ownership question.
